replacement:
* RESOLVED 2026-08-21 (was: the exponential-looking 4-byte ramp "near 0x00F0A0" inside
   IRAM_FirmwareConfig). Three corrections and a consumer.
   (a) It does not start near 0x00F0A0. 0x00F09D-0x00F0BB is a 31-byte run of zeros. The first
       word, 0x000088C1, is at 0x00F140 -- file offset 576 of
       original_ROMs/kn5000_subprogram_v142.rom.
   (b) Its left edge is exact and meaningful. DSP_Reset (0x0360A7) copies 0x91 words = 0x122 =
       290 bytes from 0x00F01E to the live effect-configuration buffer at DRAM 0x448E
       (`ld xiy,0xF01E / ld xix,0x448E / ldw bc,0x91 / ldirw`), then re-reads offset +8 of that
       source image as `ldw_d16 xiz, 61478` (= 0x00F026). 0x00F01E + 0x122 = 0x00F140: the ramp
       begins exactly where the default effect-config image ends.
   (c) Its right edge is 0x00F33F -- 128 u32 entries, 0x00F140-0x00F33F, ending at exactly
       0x7FFFFF00, the same entry count and the same terminator as DSP_MixerGain_Curve
       (0x0131CF). That edge is NOT fixed by the monotonic scan: read as unsigned, the strictly
       increasing run is 129 entries, because 0x00F340 = 0xEE9AFF00 is above 0x7FFFFF00. What
       excludes that word is that it is negative as s32 and that 0x00F340-0x00F34D does not
       continue the curve at all (0xEE9AFF00, 0x10000003, then six zero bytes), with the first
       decodable double of the libm constant pool at 0x00F34E. By contrast DSP_MixerGain_Curve's
       own edge IS self-evident: its entry 128 is 0x63000000 and breaks the run.
   (d) CONSUMER: DSP_MixerCoeff_Compute (0x03C067) reads it at three sites, all
       `lda_d16 xbc, 61760` (= 0x00F140), scaled 4*WA and 4*DE, and FP_MulAccum64s the two
       lookups against DSP_MixerGain_Curve[4*BC] before writing the product to DSP2 (MN19413)
       registers 0xD0 and 0xD3. WA, BC and DE are the three main-CPU mixer parameters held at
       DRAM 0x45B2 / 0x45B4 / 0x45B6 (CmdHandler2C global sub-commands 0x01 / 0x02 / 0x06 --
       see symbols/proposals/subcpu-region-12.txt).
   So it is an AMPLITUDE curve, the twin of DSP_MixerGain_Curve. The old guess "envelope/level
   or frequency" is half right: the "frequency" half is refuted by the 0x7FFFFF00 terminator and
   by the only proven consumer treating the value as a gain.
